facts.text: A harmonized standard is a standard officially listed under European law that gives products built to it a presumption of meeting the law; "state of the art" means the level of safety made possible by current good practice.
facts.quote: A harmonized standard is one that European law officially lists, so that a product built to it is presumed to meet the law, and "state of the art" is the legal phrase for the level of safety that current good practice makes possible.

facts.text: EU product law such as the Machinery Regulation sets general essential health and safety requirements: machines must be safe, risks reduced, and control systems reliable, without specifying how.
facts.quote: European Union (EU) product law such as the Machinery Regulation sets "essential health and safety requirements" in general words: the machine must be safe, risks reduced, control systems reliable. It does not say how.

facts.text: The European Commission asks CEN and CENELEC to write standards specifying how to meet EU product-law requirements and publishes their references in the Official Journal; listed standards are harmonized.
facts.quote: The European Commission asks the European standards bodies CEN and CENELEC to write standards that spell out the how, and publishes their references in the Official Journal. A standard on that list is "harmonized" [Chapter 3].

facts.text: Building and testing to a harmonized standard creates a presumption that the matching legal requirement is met, shifting the burden to anyone claiming otherwise.
facts.quote: build and test to a harmonized standard and the law presumes the matching requirement is met, so the burden shifts to anyone who claims otherwise.

facts.text: Great Britain copied the harmonized-standard mechanism as "designated standards"; its notice of 8 August 2026 designated the EN 474:2022 earth-moving machinery family.
facts.quote: Great Britain copied the mechanism as "designated standards"; its notice of 8 August 2026 designated the EN 474:2022 earth-moving machinery family [Chapter 3].

facts.text: The presumption of conformity extends only to the scope of the harmonized standard; EN 474 provides a presumption-of-conformity route but is not an automatic-braking performance matrix.
facts.quote: The presumption is only as wide as the standard. EN 474 gives "a presumption-of-conformity route but is not an automatic-braking performance matrix"

facts.text: Whether EN 474 or EN ISO 21815 would be harmonized under the new Machinery Regulation was not verified because the European Commission was still preparing the list in 2026.
facts.quote: whether EN 474 or EN ISO 21815 will be harmonized under the new Machinery Regulation was not verified, because the Commission was still preparing the list in 2026 [Chapter 3].

facts.text: When no harmonized standard fits, the manufacturer must apply the state of the art—what competent engineers currently know how to do—and standards usually provide evidence of that even when not harmonized.
facts.quote: "State of the art" is the fallback when no harmonized standard fits: the manufacturer must apply what competent engineers currently know how to do, and standards are the usual evidence of that even when not harmonized.

facts.text: A voluntary standard can become legally significant through the manufacturer's chosen route to demonstrate the state of the art.
facts.quote: The booklet lists "the manufacturer's chosen route to demonstrate the state of the art" as one way a voluntary standard becomes legally significant [Chapter 3].

facts.text: For the machine to be sold in the EU, the booklet recommends a standards-status checkpoint immediately before the 2027 declaration of conformity because the applicable regulation's harmonized list was unfinished in 2026.
facts.quote: The machine will be sold in the EU under a regulation whose harmonized list was unfinished in 2026, so the booklet asks for a standards-status checkpoint immediately before the 2027 declaration of conformity [Chapter 3].

facts.text: Where no harmonized standard covers automatic braking, the manufacturer's own safety case carries the weight of demonstrating safety.
facts.quote: Where no harmonized standard covers automatic braking, the manufacturer's own safety case carries the weight.
